description:
A MAN ON THE FLOOR CAN GO BACK FOR THE BALL. THREE BYTES, ONE PURPOSE. Test it FOURTH, alone, and judge this one with your EYES rather than your hands.

THE PROBLEM. Being put on the ground is the most total version of the lockout. While the current action is FallDown (0x11) or Dive (0x0f), the eligibility filter refuses Dribble outright, refuses Move outright, refuses Tackle outright - everything. Exactly one request survives, Trap, and even that is routed to the LAST cancel keyframe. Emulated through the real request chain: from the floor, only Trap starts at all, and only at frame 48 of a 64-frame test motion. So a fall is not a setback, it is a removal: the animation has to run out before you exist again.

WHAT CHANGES. Two mechanisms, same purpose.
  (1) FallDown/Dive::vf14 (0x143f00d00) picks WHICH cancel keyframe to gate on. Stock, only contact sub-kind 2 gets the FIRST key; sub-kinds 0/1/3/4 wait for the LAST. The branch at 0x143f00d71 ('jne 0x143f00d7d' after 'cmp byte [rbx+0x2bdc],2') is replaced with a 2-byte nop so every fall takes the first key.
  (2) Dribble::vf2 (0x143f99eb0) refuses outright while the current action is FallDown or Dive. Two entries of its switch byte-table at 0x143f99f60 move onto the same 'ask the cancel gate' handler that the Stagger entry already uses.
Neither part writes a pool cell and neither needs new code.

WHY THESE THREE BYTES SHIP TOGETHER. They are each inert alone, which is why this is one pack and not three. Part (1) on its own changes nothing you can feel, because while FallDown is running the eligibility filter drops every outfield request anyway - there is nothing waiting on the gate to be let through earlier. Part (2) on its own is nearly as weak, because Dribble would then be gated on the LAST keyframe, i.e. the end of the fall. Only together do they produce 'scramble up and go'.

MEASURED EFFECT (a-EMULATED, this pass, end to end through the REAL requester 0x143eb4f40). First frame the request starts, current action = FallDown, test motion with cancel keys at 16/32/48 and the end key at 64:
    request            stock     THIS PACK
    Dribble            never      16
    Trap               48         16
    (Move              never      never - that needs contact-move-out-of-stagger.json as well)

HOW IT KEEPS THE WEIGHT. The fall animation is untouched: same motion, same length, same severity selection. What moves is only the frame at which the game stops discarding your input, and it moves to the animation's OWN first cancel keyframe - a marker the animators authored, not a number invented here. You still go down, you still lose the ground, you still lose the time to frame 16. You stop losing the rest of it.

EVIDENCE.
  a-EMULATED - all rows above, on the game's own bytes under Unicorn through the real request chain 0x143eb4f40 -> Dribble::vf2 0x143f99eb0 / Trap::vf2 0x143f89ef0 -> FallDown::vf14 0x143f00d00 -> starter 0x143eb4fd0. Harness tools/emu_contact_request.py, output build/emu_contact_request_proof.txt sections 5 and 7.
  a-EMULATED - the value sweep on the Dribble table entry: 0=gated@48, 1=ALLOW-OUTRIGHT@0, 2=gated@48, 3=refuse (stock). Value 2 is used; value 1 would start the dribble on frame 0 of the fall and erase it completely.
  b-DISASSEMBLY - FallDown::vf14's keyframe selection at 0x143f00d6a-0x143f00d86 ('cmp byte [rbx+0x2bdc],2' then 'lea r9d,[rbp-1]' (last) vs 'xor r9d,r9d' (first)); Dribble::vf2's table at 0x143f99f60 with handlers at 0x143f99f50.
  NOT CLAIMED - what the contact sub-kind byte at work+0x2bdc actually means. Sub-kind 2 is the one Konami already gives the early key to; the other four are being given the same treatment without knowing what distinguishes them. That is the main reason this pack is ranked last.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE, including the CPU. Expect opposition players to get up off the floor faster too.

WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE IN ONE MATCH. After a heavy challenge that puts your man down near the ball, you should be able to reach it as he comes up, rather than watching the recovery animation finish first.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO FAR - AND THIS IS THE PACK MOST LIKELY TO LOOK WRONG RATHER THAN FEEL WRONG. Players popping up mid-tumble, clipping through the get-up, or a dribble starting while the body is still horizontal. Falls have a long authored recovery tail and cancelling into it is exactly the transition the animators never planned for. Watch the picture on the first three falls after applying. If the movement looks broken, revert - do not try to soften it, because the cancel keyframes are per-animation data and there is no scalar here to turn down.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: none directly.

COLLISIONS. All three sites verified byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE this pass (0x143f00d71=750A, 0x143f99f6f=03, 0x143f99f6d=03). No overlap with any of the 26 applied specs. Independent of the Stagger packs - verified in the emulated matrix, where this pack leaves every Stagger row at stock.

SUPERSEDES tools/data/patches/contact-falldown-cancel-early.json and tools/data/patches/contact-allow-dribble-from-falldown.json, which are the two halves of this pack shipped separately and are individually inert. Do not apply those alongside this one.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/contact-getup-from-falldown.json

patches.name: FallDown/Dive::vf14 - every fall uses the FIRST cancel keyframe, not the last
patches.note: 'jne 0x143f00d7d' -> 2-byte nop, after 'cmp byte ptr [rbx+0x2bdc], 2' inside match::anime::action::FallDown::vf14 (0x143f00d00, shared by Dive). The equal path sets idx = 0 (first channel-5 cancel key); the not-equal path set idx = count-1 (the last). Nopping the branch makes every contact sub-kind take the first key. Same instruction length, no pool cell touched.

patches.name: Dribble::vf2 - a fallen player may ask to go back to the ball
patches.note: Entry (FallDown 0x11 - 2 = 0x0f) of the switch byte-table at 0x143f99f60 inside match::anime::action::Dribble::vf2 (0x143f99eb0). Case 3 is the refuse tail at 0x143f99f45; case 2 is the existing handler at 0x143f99f1f that asks the running action's vf14 with requested kind 4 - the same case the Stagger entry (0x143f99f6e) already uses. Case 1 would also admit it but is ALLOW-OUTRIGHT (emulated: frame 0, no gate) and is deliberately NOT used.

patches.name: Dribble::vf2 - the same for a Dive
patches.note: Entry (Dive 0x0f - 2 = 0x0d) of the same table. Dive shares FallDown::vf14, so it inherits the first-keyframe change above.
